Sam (Support): FYI from Alex at Winterwell — they started seeing p99s climb on /v1/embeddings around 09:10 UTC. Customer reports a bunch of requests timing out or taking 10-30s. They say it started after a marketing campaign spike. Sam (Support): attaching their sample request patterns and account id: acct-winter-42. Alex (Customer): yes, spike was ~09:08-09:25 UTC, mostly batch embed jobs (50-200 calls/min), single-tenant. We're seeing 5% of requests > 10s. happy to provide logs. Katie (CS): adding SRE/Platform. This looks like a per-tenant tail issue rather than global. Any quick mitigation we can offer? Jay (SRE): first pass: queue depth/backpressure + noisy key. Can you share request ids? Alex (Customer): sent in DM, sample ids: req_20260315_9301, req_20260315_9312, req_20260315_9320. Sam (Support): pasted those into the thread. Jay (SRE): pulling traces now. Early signs: majority of those hit a single backend pool node and queued behind a long-running decode op. Marta (Platform): is this the pool with mixed small/bulk jobs? We recently changed batching thresholds on that pool last week. Jay (SRE): yes — pool gpu-pool-eu-west-3. I see a sudden queue bump at 09:08:40 (queue depth ~320) and some workers hit head-of-line blocking due to 1 heavy long token stream (large input). Jay (SRE): stack traces show long KV-cache memory pressure and a few OOM evictions triggering CPU fallback on some workers. DeployBot: build/serve-rt@v3.9.2 deployed 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC. Sam (Support): so noisy neighbor where one tenant's large batch/long sequence is causing others to queue — suggested mitigations? Marta (Platform): short-term: apply a per-tenant rate cap and route Winterwell to a dedicated reservation or a burst-limited queue. We can also temporarily pin them to a smaller model shard that has shorter decode times. Katie (CS): can we do a soft throttle + allowlist for reservation? Alex (Customer): we'd prefer auto-throttle on our side but need guidance. We can coordinate to ensure job sizes are chunked. Jay (SRE): proposed immediate steps: 1) create a soft throttle policy for acct-winter-42 limiting concurrent requests to 40 2) add acct-winter-42 to short-burst reservation for 10 minutes 3) enable fallback to quantized model variant for embedding endpoint (same embeddings, faster decode) Sam (Support): can you run the commands/ops? Marta (Platform): running route update now. Patch command: ```bash
# limit concurrent inflight for tenant
redwoodctl routes update --tenant acct-winter-42 --concurrency 40 --policy soft-throttle
# add to short reservation (10m)
redwoodctl reservations add --tenant acct-winter-42 --pool reserved-short --duration 10m
``` Marta (Platform): applied policy at 09:17:04 UTC. Jay (SRE): also toggled fallback to quantized variant: ```json
{"endpoint":"/v1/embeddings","model_override":"embed-base-quant-q4_0"}
``` Jay (SRE): fallback enabled at 09:17:40 UTC. Sam (Support): Alex, did you observe immediate improvement? Alex (Customer): yes — p99 dropped from ~22s to ~3.1s within 2 minutes. thank you. still seeing occasional ~5s spikes but much better. Alex (Customer): our batch runner will split bigger jobs now but would like a longer-term solution. Katie (CS): next steps for long-term: recommend reserved capacity or tenant isolation for predictable peak, plus workload profiling. Jay (SRE): ops notes: root cause = head-of-line blocking from very large single requests combined with changed batching thresholds + a heterogeneous pool. Recommendation: 1) review batching thresholds for pools serving mixed batch sizes 2) implement tenant-aware batching (prefer grouping by input length) 3) add automatic hot-tenant detection that proactively isolates when queue depth > 200 and p99 > 8s 4) expose a customer-side SDK flag to request smaller chunking. Marta (Platform): I'll file infra ticket and schedule a canary for tenant-aware batching. Ticket: INF-2026-4031 (tenant-aware-batching + hot-tenant isolation). Katie (CS): I'll follow up with Winterwell about reservation pricing and recommend a gradual reserved window for campaign spikes. Alex (Customer): appreciate the quick response. Can we get logs for the evicted worker ids? Jay (SRE): yes — attaching evicted worker ids: worker-87, worker-101, worker-142. Logs: ```
2026-03-15T09:08:42Z worker-87 OOM on KV cache, fallback to CPU slow path, decode latency +14s
2026-03-15T09:08:45Z worker-101 long-decode (seq_len=4096) blocking queue
```
Jay (SRE): we'll schedule a retrospective if infra ticket is large. Sam (Support): closing loop: soft throttle + reservation + quantized fallback helped. I'll keep thread open for any residuals. :white_check_mark:
